From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-03T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Internal — Counsel comments on ClientCorp redline (summary)

Team,

I reviewed ClientCorp's redline and discussed with external counsel. Summary of the unusual/negotiable items:

1) Subprocessor carve-out request — they want a prior notice + 30-day opt-out for any subprocessor that *could* access identifiable datasets. We should push back and propose notice + ability to object for regulated categories only.

2) Transfer mechanism — ClientCorp insists on DPF for EU->US. Counsel recommends SCCs + contract clause for periodic reassessment; escalate DPF if they take a legal lead.

3) Liability caps — standard back-and-forth; they want to broaden exceptions for exclusions tied to security incidents that are not "willful". Counsel suggests tightened definitions rather than removing caps.

4) Evidence delivery — they want SOC2 full report attached to the agreement. We can provide the summary now and full report via secure link after an NDA.

Action items I'd like on my plate:
- Rishi to confirm whether any subprocessor has EU-hosted KVS (we had one partner with EU-region storage last quarter).
- Jonas to prepare the SCC + fallback clause language.
- Olga to prepare the e-sign routing proposal (AdobeSign for EMEA + DocuSign for US counter-signed) and timing for delivery.

Short replies welcome — we should aim to send a consolidated candidate redline to ClientCorp by EOD 2026-10-05.

Marissa
Sr. Counsel (Privacy)
Redwood Inference

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, olga.petrov@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-04T14:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal — Counsel comments on ClientCorp redline (summary)

Quick update from infra:

- Subprocessors: current inventory attached. Only two subprocessors operate EU-region persistent storage for customer-managed datasets: FastCache Ltd. (EU cluster) and VectorStore GmbH (FR region). Both are covered under our standard DSPA and support SCCs.
- KV cache note: no customer PII is intentionally retained in persistent KV for any customer unless explicitly configured; we should call this out to reduce scope of their opt-out ask.

I attached a one-page technical memo to clarify where data resides and the retention defaults.

Rishi
Head of Platform Security Operations
[Attachment: RI_Subprocessor_Inventory_20261001.xlsx]

From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@clientcorp.com>, privacy-counsel@clientcorp.com, contracts@clientcorp.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-05T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed DPA candidate (Round 1 response) + e-sign routing

Jane — attaching our annotated DPA candidate that responds to the items in your redline. Highlights:

- Subprocessors: We accepted notice + 30-day objection window only for subprocessors that will process regulated categories (health/financial). For general-purpose infra subprocessors we propose notice + 10-day escalation to PI team before onboarding.
- Transfers: We propose SCCs as the primary transfer mechanism with a 180-day mutual review to consider DPF adoption if legal teams agree.
- Evidence: Attached SOC2 summary; full report available via secure transfer after NDA (link included in the cover sheet).
- Liability: We tightened the definition of "security incident" to narrow carve-outs and preserve the negotiated cap.
- E-sign routing: Per your preference, we propose AdobeSign envelope for EMEA signatories, with DocuSign used for US internal countersign to maintain our internal workflow. If EMEA legal needs a single-provider flow, we can collapse to AdobeSign end-to-end — please confirm.

Attachments: Proposed_DPA_Redline_RI_annotated.docx, Redwood_SOC2_Type2_Q2_2026_summary.pdf

Would appreciate confirmation on the e-sign preference and whether we should provide the full SOC2 under NDA now or wait until you confirm the commercial terms.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Senior Manager, Privacy & Security Operations
Redwood Inference

From: privacy-counsel@clientcorp.com
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: jane.doe@clientcorp.com, contracts@clientcorp.com
Date: 2026-10-11T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed DPA candidate (Round 1 response) + e-sign routing

Olga / Marissa — thanks for the thorough response and the SOC2 summary. A few points from our side:

- We can accept your subprocessor compromise subject to one revision: expand the 30-day objection to include subprocessors that will process "sensitive personal data" regardless of industry tag. Please add "sensitive personal data" examples in the definition.
- Transfer clause: SCCs are acceptable as the starting point. Our compliance team will look at the 180-day review clause and may request a shorter reassessment for specific datasets.
- Evidence: we'll sign an NDA to get the full SOC2; please send the DocuSign link.
- E-sign: AdobeSign preferred for EMEA execution — we will provide a contact for their legal ops. We appreciate the dual-route offer but prefer a single AdobeSign envelope if possible.

Please go ahead and share the DocuSign NDA link for the SOC2 and revise the subprocessor definition to call out "sensitive personal data" examples (race, health, biometric identifiers).

Best,
Camille Frost
Privacy Counsel, ClientCorp
[Attachment: (none)]
